analysis.title: Erratum: Fundamentals Intact, Leadership May Not Be; Lowering Target to $205
key_insights: Stifel lowers its NVDA target to $205 from $315 and reiterates Buy. The new target is 13x FY28E EPS of $15.65 (was 20x). Estimates are unchanged.

After the close on 11/11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a relationship with another NVDA executive. The Wall Street Journal reported the board is preparing to remove him as CEO. Bloomberg reported that a search firm has been engaged and an interim CEO is under consideration. Nothing has been announced, but Stifel now treats a leadership transition as its base case.
Stifel says the fundamentals are not the issue. It expects a modest F3Q27 beat on 11/17, supply remains the binding constraint, and FY28 estimates skew higher. The issue is the multiple.

F3Q guidance midpoints are revenue of $108.0B and adj-GM of 74.0%. Consensus is $108.8B revenue, 74.1% adj-GM and $2.47 adj-EPS. NVDA has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last eight quarters, by 1.5% to 5.8% and about 3.3% on average. At that average, F3Q revenue would be near $112B.
Stifel expects Vera Rubin to contribute roughly a fifth of F3Q data center revenue, based on management commentary on the F2Q call.

Management's first year-ahead outlook called for about 70% FY28 growth, with demand supporting closer to 100% and supply the constraint. FY28 consensus of $693.2B already implies about 69% growth on FY27 consensus of $410.0B, so upside requires supply to exceed the framework.

Stifel expects CFO Colette Kress to carry more of the messaging on the call. She has been cited in press reports as a possible interim CEO. Stifel would watch operating continuity, whether the 70% FY28 framework moves higher, 10-Q risk factor changes and buyback pace.

Stifel's margin estimates are 74.0% for F3Q, 71.5% for F4Q and 72.5% for FY28, against management's FY28 adj-GM indication of 72-73%. HBM pricing is contracted and renegotiated annually, so Stifel sees limited margin downside from memory. A miss is more likely to come from new-rack yields, Kyber in particular.

Supply-chain reports, unconfirmed by the company, point to NVL72 volumes shifting one to two quarters, with GB300 extended into 1H27. Stifel reads this as a Blackwell/Rubin mix question rather than a unit question, and thinks the print and the January guide are safe.

NVDA trades at about 11x FY2 P/E on Stifel's estimates and lower after hours, versus about 24-25x in January 2026. Stifel does not expect the gap to close until the board names a leader. The 13x target implies about 18% upside from the 11/11 close. High single digits is possible in a disorderly transition, which Stifel calls the principal downside case.

Export risk is moving closer to estimates. The Information reported that China- and Singapore-linked companies tied to a former Megaspeed executive acquired about $7.5B of NVDA chips, and the NYT reported a DOJ criminal inquiry into Megaspeed. These remain reports and allegations, and NVDA has not been found to have acted improperly. Stifel expects tighter customer screening across Southeast Asian channels, and revenue tied to those channels is not excluded from the outlook the way China is.
Congressional scrutiny continues, with three House committee chairs requesting a closed briefing and Rep. Mast saying a subpoena is possible.
AMD now sees its server CPU business roughly doubling in 2027, consistent with NVDA's outlook for CPU revenue to more than double in FY28.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $205 from $315 on a lower multiple of 13x FY28E EPS (was 20x), reflecting a likely leadership transition and governance and policy uncertainty. Estimates unchanged and Buy reiterated.

sector_views.rationale: Demand remains supply-gated and led by hyperscaler and AI cloud deployments, with CPU and networking attach adding content per rack.

earnings_insights: NVDA F3Q27 reports 11/17. Guidance midpoints are revenue $108.0B and adj-GM 74.0%. Consensus est is $108.8B revenue, 74.1% adj-GM and $2.47 adj-EPS. Stifel's estimates are $108.00B revenue and $2.43 adj-EPS (net).

Already reported (A): F1Q27 adj-EPS $1.87 and revenue $81.61B, F2Q27 adj-EPS $2.22 and revenue $96.22B. Stifel estimates FY27E adj-EPS $9.34 and revenue $415.0B, FY28E adj-EPS $15.65 and revenue $705.0B, FY29E adj-EPS $19.45 and revenue $895.0B.
NVDA has beaten revenue consensus in each of the last eight quarters, by 1.5% to 5.8% and about 3.3% on average. At the average, F3Q revenue would be about $112B.
Stifel's F4Q27E adj-GM is 71.5% and its FY28E adj-GM is 72.5%, against management's FY28 adj-GM range of 72-73% and a guided F4Q adj-GM bottom of 71-72%.
Stifel's FY28E revenue of $705.0B compares with consensus of $693.2B. FY27 consensus revenue is $410.0B.

trade_ideas.description: Long NVDA, Buy rating with a $205 target (13x FY28E EPS of $15.65), about 18% upside from the 11/11 close of $173.73
trade_ideas.rationale: Fundamentals are intact and supply-gated demand supports estimates skewed higher. The de-rating reflects leadership uncertainty, and 13x could prove conservative if the board names a leader the market sees as preserving continuity.
trade_ideas.risk: Board outcome on CEO leadership, tighter export controls, Rubin Ultra and Kyber yield issues, memory cost inflation, permitting and financing constraints, custom accelerator competition, digestion, and macro.

risk_factors: Outcome of the board's deliberations on CEO leadership, including timing, identity and execution of any transition and retention of senior leadership.
Tighter US export controls or enforcement actions affecting customer channels, including Southeast Asia.
Supply constraints or yield issues on new rack-scale platforms, including Rubin Ultra and Kyber.
Memory and component cost inflation pressuring gross margins beyond management's framework.
Data center permitting, power availability or customer financing constraints, including NVDA's backstop and guarantee commitments.
Competition from custom accelerators and merchant alternatives.
A digestion period following several quarters of significant investment.
vol_and_positioning: NVDA's forward P/E has compressed to about 11x FY2 EPS on Stifel's estimates, from about 24-25x in January 2026 and 13-14x in early October. Stifel says a move to high single digits is possible in a disorderly transition.
geopolitical: The 1/10/27 US-China trade truce expiry, with APEC and the G20 as two Trump-Xi touchpoints. Stifel expects policy visibility to build into mid-January rather than at the print.
Reports of a DOJ criminal inquiry into Megaspeed and of China- and Singapore-linked purchases of about $7.5B of NVDA chips, with possible tighter export screening in Southeast Asia.
Congressional scrutiny of NVDA, with three House committee chairs requesting a closed briefing and a possible subpoena per Rep. Mast.
US data center permitting after the midterms is a deployment-timing risk concentrated among smaller, less capitalized builders.

tension_points.bull_case: Fundamentals are intact. Stifel expects a modest F3Q beat, supply-gated demand and FY28 estimates skewed higher. The 13x target could prove conservative if the board names a leader the market views as preserving operating continuity.
tension_points.bear_case: A leadership change risks execution, the multiple and NVDA's standing in Washington. A disorderly transition could take the multiple to high single digits, and an extended external search would add uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A disorderly transition or a long external CEO search with senior leadership departures, or no named leader by the time of the 11/17 call.

theme_stances.key_argument: Fundamentals are intact and the de-rating reflects leadership uncertainty, so Stifel cuts the multiple but keeps Buy.
theme_stances.evidence: The fundamentals are not the issue
